title: Port Nanoleaf harnesses to owning modules and refresh pins
body:
Refs #410.

Ports all three Nanoleaf harnesses to `shared_source` and `database`, removing bridge-module arguments and rebinding. The shared CLI fixture passes an explicit state directory and no-op launch seam. It supplies synthetic legacy-hook metadata inside its disposable directory so rollback keeps exercising the real legacy-source precondition without reading personal Codex state. Existing assertions and receipt shapes remain intact.

Refreshes all three Nanoleaf pins to immutable `f3c13843f1e5431b01ddca344a91cd7484348f59`, including hashes for the new owning modules. The Pixoo pin remains `28f4875b7a0f0e57ca6f25d9971e125e927a5503`; vendored integration artifacts remain unchanged. Goal 3 coordination is recorded on #410/#407/Nanoleaf #174; Goal 3 explicitly acknowledged this immutable pin in #410.

Validation: the original scripts reproduced missing `shared_input.command`/`configure` failures against the new pin. After the port, `check-hub-shared-consumers.mjs` passes, including both projections, acknowledgments, handoff and legacy rollback. `check-session-retirement.mjs` passes for codex/desktop, codex/cli and claude/code with all 41 fixture cases. The confined standalone smoke worker completes all 11 scenarios with no scenario failures and successful process cleanup; its exit 1/nonqualified result is expected because smoke mode intentionally omits qualification sample counts. This is harness compatibility evidence, not performance qualification.

Fresh Node 24 build, types, controller TypeScript/Python/package checks, Hub tests/package, setup, Hub MCP, standalone performance tests and workflow checks pass. Workflow inventory: 18 specs, 42 archived changes, 15 workflow tests. Detailed source-only logs and receipts are retained in main `.local/evidence/gh-410-nanoleaf-harnesses/`. No application behavior, UI, installation or device operation changes; no OpenSpec delta is needed for this tooling repair.

Frozen comparison: base/merge-base `a8f85a2b265a3760072138b364cb287af30eb6bb`; head `245d03316cb518ef1598ed83309f74af4e1fa39a`; clean worktree. Both independent Standards/Specification reviews passed and were refreshed after rebase. Matching current-head CI is pending.

After the CLI base change, a fresh build and all owning shared-consumer/three-path retirement checks passed again. A focused confined worker probe exits 0 after configure/poll and checks the original receipt shape; the identical probe against the original committed worker fails on the missing configure API.

The README compatibility table now names the refreshed source pin. The owning native settings/receipt/geometry check (`check-hub-nanoleaf.mjs`) also passed against that exact Nanoleaf revision. Final candidate is based on merged #263; its unrelated test changes do not affect these harnesses. Reviews/checks are refreshed for the final head.

title: Make the dashboard a dense control surface with a home widget grid and hash routes
body:
Refs #277. Also delivers the discriminated navigation value that #247 asks for, because the hash routes need it; closing #247 is the owner's call (its "failing regression case before the fix" was not recorded as red-before-fix evidence here).

## Problem

Once signed in, the owner saw long single-column pages. The wall component page was a ten-row fact list and about twelve stacked forms, 3,624 px tall at 1,280 px wide on `main` (`ba08043`), with selects stopping at half the column. The Activity page spent its first screen on a hero and a stats strip before any session. ADR 0007 makes this dashboard the B.U.N.N.Y. shell whose starting page is a home of widgets.

## What changes

- **Home widget grid.** `apps/dashboard/src/widgets.ts` is the catalog: each widget declares ID, name, description, sizes, source kind (controller alias, hub route or read-only external source), the reads it needs and whether it has command actions, as the owner asked on 2026-09-25. The home places one component widget per registered component (health, status strip, and the same Mode and Power cards as the component page, with a link to it), then Attention, Collector and Sessions widgets. Sessions are compact rows with an inline label field and retained notices under the row. Placement is a developer decision here; #366 makes it the owner's.
- **Hash routes.** `apps/dashboard/src/routes.ts` maps `#/`, `#/component/<alias>`, `#/music/<source>` and `#/connections` to a discriminated route, so an alias of `activity` or `connections` opens only that component. A link click applies its route in the click event, ahead of the deferred `hashchange`; the back button walks the history; an unknown address shows a not-found message; the skip link focuses the main column without touching the hash. A route bookmark opens signed in on its page under #419's trusted-loopback sign-in.
- **Dense component page.** A one-line status strip (mode, power, brightness, observation age, pending; observed color for LIFX), the rare facts behind a Details disclosure, #414's device art for Nanoleaf, and every control as a card in a grid that fills the width: Mode with Reapply or Start Monitor, Power, Brightness, Media with the Media switch, Scenes with the Free switch, LIFX Color and Color temperature. Each card keeps one short visible state line; longer guidance sits behind a Help disclosure. Nanoleaf's settings and mappings sit in one Assignments panel (with #412's read-only gating and #414's picked element), the Pixoo view form in one Monitor panel. `apps/dashboard/src/controls.tsx` holds the form and action primitives and the cards over one `deviceControls` read, so a card renders identically on the home and the page and shares one lifecycle state per component and control between them.
- **Connections** is a two-card page; **login** is one line and the token disclosure, keeping #419's signed-out state, Sign in, alert and Sign in again.
- **After the merges with main:** #419's trusted-loopback sign-in also covers route bookmarks (`#/component/pixel` opens signed in on that page), #414's device art sits on the Nanoleaf page above the cards with its picked element flowing into the Assignments panel, and #433's LIFX Work/Quiet/Free mode control and Switch to Free sit in the LIFX Mode and Color cards.
- **Scale tokens.** The application skin defines `--space-xxs` to `--space-xl` and the type sizes; `style.css` reads its colors, spacing steps and type sizes only through tokens (column tracks, control heights and breakpoints stay structural).

## Owner decision on the design candidate (2026-09-25)

After reviewing the candidate frames the owner asked for fewer clicks: no Apply button anywhere, sliders sending once on release, and the on/off dropdown as a button, delivered in this PR before approval. What that changed:

- A select sends a pointer choice at once and a keyboard step after a short pause, on Enter or on blur, so arrowing through options sends only the one stopped on. A slider sends once when the pointer releases it, or after a pause following a keyboard step or a script change, never mid-drag. A color picker sends when it closes. A text field sends when it is left or on Enter, and only while the browser's constraints hold. Power is one button naming the action left (Turn on or Turn off; both when power is unknown). Choosing a playlist starts it; choosing a scene activates it.
- Kept: one guarded command per gesture from a fresh read, typed rejections that change nothing, no automatic retry, the uncertain lock with its explicit reload, capability, permission and read-only Nanoleaf gating, accessible names, keyboard operation, reduced motion, axe at desktop and 390 px, and the served assets under the same CSP.
- Retired: the draft-and-conflict rule for device controls. A rejected change shows the current value again with its status. The form wording in `lifecycle.ts` changed accordingly ("Your edit is kept" is gone; a retryable rejection says "Change it again to try with current values").
- The `unified-dashboard` spec is modified for it (General device controls, Content controls, Protected explicit integration commands, Reconnect, Shared command lifecycle, Power control, LIFX views and the #412 read-only rule), with the archived change's delta carrying the MODIFIED requirements. The issue's Work assessment records the decision.

**Please confirm on this PR that one approval of the current candidate covers both steps of the issue (design candidate and implemented candidate).** The hand-built static mock of step 1 was replaced by static HTML and screenshots of the built candidate, because you chose on 2026-09-25 to settle the page split from the built candidate.

## Measurements (fake-controller fixture, head `9ef42f2`)

| View | Before (`ba08043`) | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wall page height at 1,280 px | 3,624 px | 1,849 px, of which the #414 device art figure is about 470 px; it counts toward the 2,000 px budget |
| Pixel page height at 1,280 px | 2,404 px | 971 px |
| Wall page height at 390 px | 4,710 px | 2,669 px |
| Home at 1,440 px | hero, stats and one session in the first screen | home, pixel and Connections fit one 1,000 px screen; every component widget, its quick actions and the sessions widget start in the first screen (asserted) |
| Controls' reach across the main column at 1,440 px | selects stopped near 50% | at least 70% on the home, wall and pixel pages (asserted); four cards per row |

## Design candidate and UI approval

Static HTML and full-page screenshots at 1,440 px and 390 px for login, home, wall, pixel and Connections (ten frames plus `manifest.json`, revision `9ef42f2`) are under `.local/evidence/gh-277-dense-dashboard/design-candidate/` in the owner's checkout, outside Git. They show fixture data and no physical result.

**Owner approval of this UI candidate is required before merge and is pending.** Any later change to this UI renews the approval. The final page split (everything on the home versus a page per component) is settled from this candidate: a page per component, with the home showing every component's everyday widgets.

## Acceptance evidence (candidate `9ef42f2`)

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Home shows every registered component as a widget with its status and quick actions on the first screen at 1,440 px | `tests/browser.mjs` asserts every `component-status` widget and the sessions widget start within the viewport and the wall and pixel widgets' controls end inside it; `home-1440.png` |
| Owner approves the design candidate, then the implemented candidate | Pending, see above |
| Wall page under 2,000 px at 1,280 px; no view with an empty right half at 1,440 px | `tests/browser.mjs` asserts wall and pixel heights under 2,000 px (receipt: 1,849 and 971) and control reach of at least 70% on home, wall and pixel; Connections cards side by side; now playing spans the width; measurements cover the four views plus wall and pixel |
| `npm run test:dashboard`, browser and matrix checks, `retirement.mjs`, `style.test.mjs` and the hub dashboard test pass | Local checks below; Depot CI |
| Style guide §7 and §12 updated with measurements | `docs/application-ui-style-guide.md` §4.1, §7, §8, §12 |
| OpenSpec: `unified-dashboard` gains routing and layout requirements; approval requirement unchanged | `gh-277-dense-control-surface` (proposal, specs delta with ADDED and MODIFIED sections, design, tasks), synchronized and archived on this branch; "Accessible verified candidate" untouched |
| Protections kept (see the owner decision section) | Browser, matrix (20 scenarios, including the home quick-action and gesture scenarios), retirement, local-controllers, trusted and art suites; `style.test.mjs`; `apps/hub/tests/dashboard.test.mjs`; the bundle contains no `style=` |
| #247: distinct navigation kinds, both built-in pages reachable beside `activity` and `connections` aliases, keyboard activation | `tests/routes.test.mjs`; `tests/browser.mjs` alias block (click, Enter, `aria-current`, back button); red-before-fix evidence not recorded |

## Local checks

Every chain below is Node 24.21.0, exit 0 for each command: `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:contracts:built`, `npm run test:contracts:python`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow`, `npm run test:dashboard` (50 pass: client, lifecycle, routes, widgets, art, style), `npm run test:hub:built`, `npm run test:hub:package:built`, `npm run test:dashboard:browser` (browser, matrix with 20 scenarios, retirement, local-controllers, trusted, art). Chains ran on `24feafc` (checks-1), `d35519c` (checks-2), `0300479` (checks-3), `67f6b9c` (checks-4), `5e433c3` (checks-5) and `9ef42f2` (checks-6): all exit 0. The OpenSpec change was validated with `--strict`, synchronized into `openspec/specs/unified-dashboard/spec.md` and archived; `openspec validate --specs --strict` and `--archived` pass at `9ef42f2`. Logs under `.local/evidence/gh-277-dense-dashboard/checks-*/` in the owner's checkout.

## UI approval scope

All of `apps/dashboard` is application UI: every view changes, and the login page changes on top of #419's. Human approval of this candidate is required and pending (see above). No work-guide content changes.

## Independent review

All reviewers are read-only fresh contexts on `opus` (self-reported Opus 5.5, effort unknown), one for Standards and one for Specification, resumed with each new frozen comparison.

- **Round 1 (`32fb03e...d35519c`)**: Standards changes required (S1 P1 skip link changed the route, S2 P2 per-instance lock, S3 to S6 P3); Specification changes required (F1 P1 same lock and lost drafts, F2 P2 no home quick-action test, F3 to F8 P3).
- **Round 2 (`32fb03e...0300479`)**, after the corrections and the owner's no-Apply decision: S1 to S6 resolved (S5 partly); new S7 P2 slider sends mid-drag, S8 P2 keyboard steps on a select send per step, S9 to S12 P3. Specification: F1 to F8 resolved or pending record; new F9 P2 and F10 P2 (the same two defects), F11 to F15 P3.
- **Round 3 (`47b9f62...67f6b9c`)**, after merging #419 and #414: Standards approve (S7 to S12 resolved; new S13 to S15 P3). Specification changes required for records only (F9 to F12, F14, F15 resolved; F13 record, F16 to F18 P3).
- **Round 4 (`6b561ba...5e433c3`)**, after merging #433: Standards approve (S13 to S15 and F17 resolved; new S16 to S18 P3). Specification changes required: F19 P2, a conflict resolution that left two normative paragraphs in the Content controls requirement; F20 P3 spec lag; F13 pending.
- **Round 5 (`6b561ba...9ef42f2`)**: Standards approve (S16 to S18 resolved; new S19 P3, recorded below); Specification approve (F19 and F20 resolved; F13 closed by this body). No P0 to P2 finding remains.

Dispositions of the P3 findings that stay recorded rather than changed: S5 (the same-event page-switch check cannot distinguish a hashchange-only router; the click handler is inspected) and the control-reach metric taking the widest control (it still rejects the base layout); F7 (measurements cover the four views plus wall and pixel; now playing spans the width); F17 for selects other than the acknowledgment (the 300 ms pause is the owner's fewer-clicks rule; a screen-reader user stepping slowly through a mode select still sends the option they pause on); S17's popup-Enter path (unverified in Chromium; blur still commits); S19 (the keyboard acknowledgment check reads the page text after the pause rather than the monitor snapshot, so a regression to a pause commit is caught only when the local round trip is fast).

## CI and merge

- Base `main` at `6b561baf3698415740184b702fc73107daec9022` (equal to the merge-base), head `9ef42f22a3a213122835c352746f980474150c83`, `git diff 6b561ba 9ef42f2`, clean worktree.
- Depot CI succeeded from `depot-code-access` on the exact head `9ef42f2`: Workflow checks 108341385938, Contracts and state Python 3.12 108341379951 and 3.14 108341381282, MCP 108341382679, Dashboard browser and contracts 108341384789, Work guide build and browser checks 108341378508 (earlier heads `d35519c` and `5e433c3` were green too).
- Merge waits on one gate: the owner's UI approval of this candidate, with the one-approval confirmation above. Then a guarded squash merge with `--match-head-commit 9ef42f2`, main CI readback and issue closure.
